# Evaluated Applications

> An embedded SQL database that learns from its queries, and small language models that talk through one shared wave. .NET libraries and tools to try now. Proprietary. Every package ships as a compiled library. Evaluation and non-commercial development or testing are permitted; commercial, production or revenue-generating use needs a commercial licence from the owner.

Updated: 2026-11-03

## Products

- [Phasor](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/phasor/): Build stores that answer exactly, replicas that sync by their differences and tables that repair themselves. One pass applies a thousand operators. `dotnet add package EvaluatedApplications.Phasor` (release 2.23.0).
- [EvalApp](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/evalapp/): Run everything at once without overloading anything. Gates on every resource, sagas that undo failures, and a tuner that finds the right speed. `dotnet add package EvaluatedApplications.EvalApp` (release 4.4.2).
- [HoloDb](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/holodb/): An embedded SQL database that learns from the queries it serves and keeps only what pays. Every answer is exact, with ACID and no index to design. `dotnet add package EvaluatedApplications.HoloDb` (release 9.0.0).
- [AlgFormer](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/algformer/): A population of small holographic language models that talk through a shared wave, in pure managed code. `dotnet add package EvaluatedApplications.AlgFormer` (release 3.4.0).
- [Prose](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/prose/): Three novels in, nearly two thousand checked new sentences out. Mines grammar into HoloDb and recombines it into text and question and answer pairs. `dotnet add package EvaluatedApplications.Prose` (release 1.5.0).
- [HoloGenome](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/hologenome/): Turn DNA into a vector that winds like the real helix, then check it against laboratory measurements it never saw. The wins and the losses are published. `dotnet add package EvaluatedApplications.HoloGenome` (release 0.2.0).
- [Tracer](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/tracer/): Send a whole crowd to one exit with a single search. Navmesh pathfinding with dynamic obstacles, line of sight and combat. `dotnet add package EvaluatedApplications.Tracer` (release 2.0.4).
- [HoloVoxel](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/holovoxel/): Voxel worlds that stay crisp up close and cost almost nothing far away, with no mesh tiers and no popping. `dotnet add package EvaluatedApplications.HoloVoxel` (release 1.5.2).
- [Blazier](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/blazier/): Blazor pages that read at once and download .NET only when a visitor presses Start, with long C# jobs in a Web Worker. `dotnet add package EvaluatedApplications.Blazier` (release 1.1.0).

## Tools

- [Umbrarium, preset demo](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/umbrarium/): The real Umbrarium dashboard computing exact answers over up to three million generated rows, entirely inside your browser tab. Click a chart to slice the rest, or run your own SQL. Powered by HoloDb.
- [Doctrine](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/tools/doctrine/): Send soldiers down three lanes toward the enemy castle. The battle runs on a navigation mesh and pauses every 30 seconds so you can choose what to send next. Play the computer, or another person through a public relay, with no accounts. Powered by Phasor, Tracer and EvalApp.
- [The Helix](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/tools/helix/): Paste DNA sequences and a column of measurements and see the double helix in the numbers: a score graded in your browser, with the controls that would expose a false win shown beside it. Powered by HoloGenome.
- [The Analyst](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/tools/analyst/): Paste any data and profile it with a real SQL database in your browser: types, distributions, anomalies and hidden entities, then query it at a live SQL prompt. Powered by HoloDb.
- [Prose](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/tools/prose/): Paste in a body of text, mine its grammar in your browser, and recombine it into sentences and question and answer pairs for a training corpus. Powered by Prose, HoloDb and AlgFormer.
- [Council Spending Scanner](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/tools/council-spending/): English councils' published spending data, prepared ahead of time and opened one month at a time, with the same mechanical checks for every council.

## Games

- [All games](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/games/): games that run in your browser tab on our libraries.
- [Doctrine](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/games/doctrine/): Send your soldiers down the lanes and take their castle. A lane battle between two castles. Every soldier is its own body on a navigation mesh, and every 30 seconds the battle pauses so you can choose what to send and how to order it. Play the computer, or another person online. Modes: Solo and Two players. Play it at https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/tools/doctrine/. Powered by Phasor, Tracer and EvalApp.

## Evidence

- [Many small models, one wave: the evidence](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/algformer/evidence/): Six atoms that each see about a sixth of the text and share the medium score 2.99 bits per character. One atom that sees all of it scores 3.38, and the same six atoms without the medium score 4.33. At width 32, a pair scores 3.47 when the loss reaches the atoms through the notes they wrote and 3.84 when the writers are frozen.
- [What attention costs](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/algformer/evidence/cost/): At the same shape and the same parameter count, reading a 1,984-token prompt takes 182 ms with softmax attention and 7.08 ms with holographic attention. Each further token takes 181 µs against 3.60 µs, and the serve cache holds 2,253 KB against 3.40 KB. Softmax reading grows with the square of the length (exponent 1.9) and holographic reading grows in step with it (1.0).
- [What a visitor waits for](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/blazier/evidence/): On the sample app the static page downloads 6.8 KB before the visitor acts, against 2.8 MB when the same app boots the usual way. Real content is on screen in 72 to 100 ms on desktop and 416 to 484 ms on the phone profile, against 748 to 1,165 ms and 13.2 to 15.5 s. After the visitor presses Start the runtime takes 710 to 1,170 ms on desktop and 12.7 to 15.4 s on the phone profile to reach a working page, the same wait as the usual boot.
- [What a gate bound does](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/evalapp/evidence/): The gate never admitted more downloads than its bound: in every recorded run the most in flight equalled the bound. The time to finish 24 queued jobs fell from 1,113 ms at a bound of 1 to 139 ms at 8, then rose again to 410 ms when all 24 ran at once, because the simulated service slows when it is crowded.
- [What HoloDb learns, and how it is tested](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/holodb/evidence/): After single-row updates and deletes the next sweep reads 6 blocks with learned records that adjust, against 60 and 51 when updates drop them, and 6 against 366 after consolidation. A wrong answer is the one failure a database cannot afford, so the tests try to make HoloDb wrong: across 8 customer runs and 158 sessions it compared 249 million rows against SQLite and recovered 46 times after a kill or a power cut, 37 times to the state before the interrupted write, 9 times to the state after, and never to a state between.
- [How HoloGenome scores against the lab](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/hologenome/evidence/): A linear readout trained on 12,472 random-sequence constructs and tested on 82,368 yeast-gene constructs (no shared sequence, forward or reverse complement) scores r = 0.529 with vectors that use the measured twist, against 0.483 with one constant twist (difference 0.046, 95% interval 0.041 to 0.050). Adding the local-shape layer lifts it to 0.600, a further 0.071. A small phasor model that chose its own period, starting from 12 bases, settled at 10.49, 10.51, 10.48 and 10.51 bases per turn on four independent libraries, against the crystallographic 10.534. The best trained network scores higher: the 22-parameter fit trails it by 0.28 to 0.39.
- [Detail against components read](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/holovoxel/evidence/): One 16 by 16 chunk stored as a single hologram decodes 98.4 percent of its cells correctly at the full budget of 8,192 components, 131,072 bytes and 17.0 ms. Reading fewer components is cheaper and fuzzier: 67.1 percent at 1,568 components, and 19.5 percent at 24, which takes 384 bytes and 0.09 ms.
- [Exact recall and refusal](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/phasor/evidence/): At equal storage the exact key view recovered 64 items with no errors where holographic reduced representations held 95 percent or better only up to 4. Past capacity the exact store refused every time, while the baseline answered wrongly every time.
- [Pleroma costs and checks](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/phasor/evidence/costs/): A superposed kernel applies in 0.17 to 0.44 ms on a 10,464-cell store whether it holds 1 or 10,368 elements, and the repair and corruption checks recovered or detected every case tried.
- [Generated sentences pass the gate](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/prose/evidence/): Of 2,000 sentences requested in one run, 1,966 different ones came back. Every one passed the package's validity gate on a fresh parse, and every word in every one was observed in the corpus.

## Research

- [Fifty reads, one store](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/research/one-store-many-reads/): One fixed-size array of exact integers. Counts, order, parity, time and nearest words, each in a single pass. When it is full, it refuses instead of guessing.
- [Nobody Read the Warning](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/research/nobody-read-the-warning/): An argument that the surviving accounts of collapsed civilisations record a loss of effective independence, which the design effect describes, and that sacred transmission preserved the accounts while removing their comprehension.

## Company

- [About Evaluated Applications](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/about/): An independent AI research lab in England. What it builds, how the results are reported, and where to find them.
- [Partner with us](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/partner/): Libraries that run in the browser mean no server, no GPU bill and no user data leaving the device. Our libraries are the stack for that, and we pay you to build on them.
- [Licence](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/licence/): Commercial licence for commercial use. Evaluation and non-commercial use are permitted.
- [For agents and other automated readers](https://evaluatedapplications.github.io/ai/): what HoloFormer and Pleroma are, what has been measured, where the packages and docs are, and where to send enquiries
- [NuGet profile](https://www.nuget.org/profiles/evaluatedapplications): every package we publish
- Contact: dongyang.stephen.chen@gmail.com
